title: Merge latch playbook (scratch)
content:
Quick context
- Working notes for a light-weight "latch" pattern to gate risky merges on small fast checks before and after merge.
- Goal: reduce mid-day incidents caused by subtle runtime changes while keeping throughput of small PRs.
- This is a personal scratchpad; not final.

Hypothesis / when to use latch
- Use for PRs that touch: runtime scheduling, batching, kv-cache hits, kernel selection, or observable-critical paths.
- Skip for pure docs/typo/README or trivial UI copy changes.
- Prefer latch for PRs > 15 LOC in critical modules or changes that touch config defaults.

Concept: "latch" flow (lightweight)
1) Pre-merge checklist (author) — should be in PR description as a short table:
   - CI passing (unit + fmt) — ✅
   - Small local perf smoke: run lightweight harness (script: tools/local-smoke.sh) — report median latency baseline vs branch — attach results snippet.
   - Sanity run of a smoke integration that covers batching path (~30s) — note any errors.
2) Reviewer quick checks (5-10min) — reviewer tags one of: green / needs-sanity / blocked:
   - Check intended change list; if touching runtime/routing, pull locally and run smoke harness (instructions below).
   - Confirm there is either a unit test or a documented risk/mitigation in PR.
3) Latch deployment (post-merge auto): a small canary rollout for 10 minutes with two controls:
   - Canary config: route 3% requests for 10 minutes to new revision on dedicated staging pool (or labeled node).
   - Observe latency P50/P95, error rate, and kv-cache hit ratio. If any metric regresses >20% relative (P95 latency or error rate), auto-fail and rollback.

Quick commands / local harness
- tools/local-smoke.sh --model llama-13b --prompt test/sample_batch.txt --concurrency 2 --duration 30
- ./bin/perf-check --compare baseline.json branch.json --metrics p50 p95 error_rate cache_hit
- Notes: harness should run in a small container that mimics batching path; it's intentionally fast and noisy but catches obvious regressions.

Rollback / mitigation playbook
- If canary fails (alert fired):
  1) Immediately flip traffic off new revision (console -> rollback button) or run: infra/ops/cut_traffic.sh --target old
  2) Post a short summary to slack:#deploys-general with PR link and metric diffs, tag oncall.
  3) Reopen PR with clear repro + failing harness artifacts.
  4) If rollback not trivial (data migrations, config drift), escalate to oncall SRE and author.

Reviewer heuristics (mental checklist)
- Did author change default config values? If yes, require a short note on risk and timeout values.
- Does change touch sequences longer than 1024 tokens or change kernel selection logic? Ask for perf numbers.
- Are there new loops that can cause O(n^2) allocation? Grep for nested for-loops over tokens in the diff.
- Look for hidden feature flags toggled without follow-up rollout steps.

Tests to require (minimum)
- Unit tests for any non-trivial logic (>= 1 new test file or clear coverage in existing tests).
- A smoke integration test that runs in CI with a short timeout (30s) — acceptable to be flaky but should be green locally.
- For quantization/ops changes: run quantized model smoke and compare outputs to baseline for drift > 2% mismatched tokens on sample set.

Observability checklist (post-merge watch window 30m)
- dashboards to watch: serving/runtime-latency, serving/error-rate, kv-cache/hit-rate, batch-size/dist
- look for 3x increase in tail latency, sustained error rate >0.5% absolute, or cache hit drop >10% relative.
- Check logs for new stack traces; sample 1-2 traces and annotate PR.

Open questions / TODO
- Should latch be enforced automatically on all merges touching specific paths? (e.g., engine/ or runtime/)
- How to automate prefix/KV cache smoke without having to run full model? Could we mock evaluation with a small fixture model?
- Integration with PR CI: add a lightweight gate that triggers harness on push to branch and posts results as a status.

Short example PR blurb to copy (author)
- "Summary: small change to request batching allocation to avoid early flush in edge-case. Risk: may change latency P95 under heavy fan-in. Local smoke attached (tools/local-smoke.out). Recommend latch on merge to canary for 10m. Tests: unit + smoke."

Notes to self
- I tried this last week on a small routing fix and it caught an inadvertent double-allocation that would have increased memory by ~8% at spike. Saved a roll-forward.
- Keep the harness lightweight; dev friction kills adoption.

Example artifacts to attach in PR (one-liners)
- baseline.json (perf run)
- branch.json (perf run)
- smoke.log (30s harness)
- small screencap showing console canary config change (optional)

Links / references (internal)
- GH example PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2741 (annotated)
- Long-form rollback runbook: confluence.redwood/internal/rollback-runbook (TBD)

End of scratchpad — refine into a formal playbook if we get buy-in from SRE and console teams.

-- Amira
